sentences.text: The thesis's central claim, buying because Jensen Huang is gone, is unsupported on this record: the 8-K confirms the resignation, but nothing in the record connects his departure to the value of the business.
Every financial figure ends with the quarter ended 2026-07-26 and the valuation is priced at 2026-09-30, so the record cannot show how either the business or the price absorbed the departure.

The supporting financial claims split: the gross-margin streak holds and quarterly revenue growth sped up, but revenue did not double in fiscal 2026 and free cash flow fell short of net income, so the thesis's operating case is mixed rather than uniformly strong.

Growth is not the binding constraint for the price: at 2026-09-30 it needs 13.4% a year against the newest quarter's 105.9%, but that arithmetic leans most on a 65.2% operating margin held every year, which is exactly what a leadership change could threaten.

The 28.5× earnings multiple rests on earnings that are converting to cash at only 0.70x over four quarters and 0.40x in the latest quarter, so the price is paying for profit that is increasingly sitting in receivables and inventory.
A careful investor would want the first 10-Q covering quarters after the resignation, an 8-K naming a permanent CEO, and evidence that the receivables and inventory build is unwinding.
The claim is a cause the filings cannot test: the departure is a fact, but the step from it to a reason to buy has no backing, because the newest quarter and the price date both precede it.
Its favourable corollaries describe a quarter run under Huang, so they cannot show that his absence helps, and the free cash flow margin corollary failed anyway, with a margin of -6.6 points.

What the record does show is a broad transition, with an interim CEO drawn from the CFO role, a retiring head of worldwide field operations and an earlier Chief Accounting Officer retirement, and that is evidence of turnover, not of improvement.
The new leadership inherits an exceptional margin position: gross margin ranks 4 of 63 among SIC 3674 filers, and the 70% streak has room of 1.69x a typical move in its tightest quarter.
Data Center growth of +116.6% outpaced the company's +105.9%, and deferred revenue grew +215.1%, which leans toward demand running ahead of shipments in the newest quarter.
Across the full grid the price needs between 6.5% and 19.7% a year, all far below the growth the latest quarter shows, so the valuation does not require the current pace to last.
Free cash flow ran $65.87B below net income over the four quarters to Q2 FY2027, as receivables rose $35.25B and inventory rose $16.61B, and cash conversion ranks 32 of 38 among SIC 3674 peers.

Inventory now covers 119.3 days against 105.6 a year before, and the last time inventory and purchase obligations went wrong, the H20 charge cut gross margin to 60.5%, so the margin streak the price depends on has a known failure mode.

Even the modest 13.4% implied growth was matched by 0 of 40 ten-year spans of filers at this size, and at the industry's 90th-percentile margin of 26.6% the price would need 28.1% a year, so the price leans heavily on margin persistence through a leadership change.
The first 10-Q after the resignation shows quarterly gross margin still above 70%.
Quarterly operating margin in that 10-Q stays above 50%.
An 8-K names a permanent Chief Executive Officer in place of the interim appointment.
Accounts receivable fall below the $63.06B of Q2 FY2027.
Inventory falls below the $31.57B of Q2 FY2027.
Quarterly free cash flow rises above the $21.40B of Q2 FY2027.
A post-resignation 10-Q shows quarterly gross margin below 70%.
An 8-K or 10-Q discloses an excess-inventory or purchase-obligation charge like the H20 charge.
Quarterly revenue falls below the $96.22B of Q2 FY2027.
